silent.title: The machine is not responding
silent.message: {{mudos}} of {{total}} points are returning no reading right now. When the VFD stops, it stops publishing speed, and without speed the module cannot compute RMS velocity: every vRMS is lost, while acceleration and peak survive because they are measured without knowing the running speed. What you see below does not describe a quiet machine: it describes a silent one.

speed.title: Shaft speed
speed.notPublished: The VFD is not publishing the speed, so the shaft is drawn still. That does not mean the machine is stopped: it means it is not on record.
speed.stopped: The VFD publishes zero: the machine is stopped.
speed.isoApplies: Above the {{rpm}} rpm at which ISO 10816 starts to apply, so the RMS velocity verdict holds (warning {{aviso}} mm/s, alarm {{alarma}} mm/s).
speed.isoBelow: Below {{rpm}} rpm: the rotational frequency falls outside the band ISO 10816 measures, so the standard does not apply and the bearings come out without a criterion.
speed.compressed: The rotation in the scene is compressed: at a real 3,475 rpm a mesh spinning 60 times a second would look still, or backwards. It conveys that it turns and roughly how much, not the exact speed.

axes.title: Only the vertical axis is measured
axes.intro: The three probes are mounted vertically, and only vertically. In the scene, the green arrow is what is measured; the two grey ones are the directions that are missing.
axes.axial: Without the axial one, a coupling misalignment may not show up: that is where it shows most.
axes.radial: Without the second radial one, unbalance and looseness look identical — what separates them is the ratio between the two.
axes.standard: {{norma}}, so this sampling does not comply with that standard.
axes.isoStillValid: The ISO 10816-1 Class I severity criterion on RMS velocity is used and does hold; what does not hold is presenting this as an assessment compliant with ISO 20816.

missing.title: What the scene cannot draw
missing.intro: The rig is mounted on slotted profile: the pillow blocks and the disc move, so their spacing is not a constant of the machine. What is still to be measured:
missing.spacing: Distance between pillow blocks, and the disc position relative to them.
missing.shaft: Shaft diameter. Without it there is no critical speed to compute.
missing.bearings: Bearing model of the two pillow blocks. Without it there is no BPFO, BPFI, BSF or FTF.
missing.onlyDimension: The only dimension on record is the shaft’s {{cm}} cm, and it comes with a caveat: {{reserva}}. That is why the scene is at reading scale and not real scale — it cannot be measured on.

probe.mounting: {{fabricante}} {{modelo}} probe, {{sensibilidad}} mV/g, {{montaje}} mounting and vertical orientation.
probe.bearingUnknown: Bearing not identified: without its reference BPFO, BPFI and FTF cannot be computed, so this bearing has no frequency-based bearing diagnosis.

config.title: Configuration · Plant
config.sub: Which machines the dashboard knows, and with which ICONICS signals
config.none: No machines have been configured yet.
config.noneHint: Machines that ship with the dashboard are not listed here: they are written in code and are not configured from this screen.
config.stateUnknownHint: Nobody has checked yet whether its points still exist. This is not a failure: it simply has not been checked.
config.readOnly: Everything configured here is read-only access
config.readOnlyWhy: Marking a variable as writable is a decision with consequences on the plant and is not taken from this screen. Machines are registered by marking the ICONICS tree; their series are verified by probing them afterwards.
config.probeResult: {{verificadas}} of {{total}} series verified as their own
config.probeConstant: Of these, {{constantes}} are constants recorded by the historian: they have not changed, and cannot be told apart from an identical one
config.probeShared: Their series is indistinguishable from another signal's (same values at every timestamp): it may be a historian cross-wiring or sources that genuinely coincide; until checked, they promise no history:
config.probeNotSaved: Nothing was recorded: what was known before is kept
config.stateDEGRADED: Some of its points are missing in ICONICS
config.stateINVALID: None of its points exist any more
config.notSaved: Could not check: what was known before is kept

editor.newTitle: New machine from the ICONICS tree
editor.intro: Mark the assets and variables that belong to this machine. Marking an asset marks all its variables; then unmark what does not belong.
editor.fieldIdHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is how previous cases and the assistant name it, and it cannot be changed later.
editor.fieldPlcHint: It is what tells whether two machines are separate installations.
editor.fieldLimitsHint: One per line. What the operator knows and the dashboard cannot infer; the assistant quotes them. The ones the validation detects are added on their own and are not edited here.
editor.fieldLimitsPlaceholder: The motor runs with no load coupled: vibrations that only appear under load cannot be observed.
editor.rootHistoryHint: The historian name cannot be derived from the live name: type it here and it is paired by name.
editor.othersHint: The type recognizes none of their variables. They are offered anyway: if one belongs to the machine, mark it.
editor.loadFailed: This branch could not be read
editor.ambiguous: Several tags with this name: choose one
editor.alarmsListed: Alarms the area lists but does not deliver
editor.actionsHint: Not offered: they are writes, and writing is deny by default.
editor.noHistoryRoot: Without a historian group there are no series to pair. Type it above and explore again.
editor.noAlarmArea: Without an alarm area there are no counters to include.
editor.missingTitle: Saved variables that are no longer in the tree
editor.missingHint: They are not deleted on their own: it may be a network outage or a rename on the server. Unmark them to remove them, or leave them if they will come back.
editor.uncheckedTitle: Saved variables whose branch could not be read
